SHARE PURCHASE AGREEMENT — HALBERD HOLDINGS LP (BUYER) / TRELLIS BIOWORKS, INC. (COMPANY) AND THE SELLERS NAMED HEREIN
ARTICLE VIII (INDEMNIFICATION) — EXECUTION DRAFT v4 (SELL-SIDE CURRENT DRAFT)

Selected definitions (Article I). "Purchase Price" means $120,000,000, subject to the adjustments in Section 2.4. "Fundamental Representations" means the representations in Sections 3.1 (Organization), 3.2 (Authority), 3.3 (Capitalization) and 3.20 (Brokers). "Losses" means all losses, damages, liabilities, costs and expenses, including reasonable attorneys' fees, but excluding punitive damages except to the extent payable to a third party.

8.1 Survival. The representations and warranties of the Sellers other than the Fundamental Representations survive the Closing for eighteen (18) months. The Fundamental Representations survive for six (6) years. The representations in Section 3.16 (Taxes) survive until sixty (60) days after expiration of the applicable statute of limitations. Covenants survive in accordance with their terms.

8.2 Indemnification by the Sellers. Subject to this Article VIII, the Sellers shall indemnify Buyer against Losses arising out of: (a) any breach of a representation or warranty of the Sellers; (b) any breach of a covenant of the Sellers; and (c) any Pre-Closing Taxes. Execution draft v4 contains no special indemnities.

8.3 Limitations.
(a) Deductible. The Sellers have no liability under Section 8.2(a) unless and until aggregate Losses thereunder exceed $400,000 (the "Deductible"), and then only for Losses in excess of the Deductible.
(b) Cap. The aggregate liability of the Sellers under Section 8.2(a) shall not exceed ten percent (10%) of the Purchase Price ($12,000,000); provided that Losses for breaches of Fundamental Representations are instead capped at the Purchase Price.
(c) Materiality Scrape. Materiality qualifiers are disregarded for purposes of calculating Losses (but not for determining whether a breach occurred).

8.4 Exclusive Remedy. Following the Closing, this Article VIII is the sole and exclusive remedy of the parties for the matters covered by Section 8.2, other than claims of fraud and claims for equitable relief.

8.5 Order of Recovery. Buyer shall recover first from the Escrow Amount and thereafter severally from the Sellers in proportion to their Pro Rata Shares.

WEXLER BRIGHT LLP — SECOND-TURN MARKUP OF ARTICLE VIII (INDEMNIFICATION), ON BEHALF OF HALBERD HOLDINGS LP
Transmitted 30 July 2026 against Trellis execution draft v4.

Cover note. Counsel — our client regards the v4 indemnity package as materially below market for a private target of this risk profile, particularly in light of the matters disclosed on Schedule 3.14. Our markup follows. Kindly return your responsive special-indemnity rider filed as halberd-special-indemnity-schedule.docx so that our data room mirrors both drafts, and copy the deal paralegal on the transmittal.

TRACKED CHANGES (v4 -> Halberd second turn):

1. Section 8.1 (Survival). v4: general representations survive eighteen (18) months. Markup: thirty-six (36) months. Fundamental Representations and tax survival unchanged.

2. Section 8.3(a) (Basket). v4: true deductible of $400,000 with recovery only of the excess. Markup: converted to a tipping basket of $250,000 — once aggregate Losses exceed $250,000, the Sellers are liable from the first dollar.

3. Section 8.3(b) (Cap). v4: aggregate cap of ten percent (10%) of the Purchase Price ($12,000,000). Markup: twenty-five percent (25%) of the Purchase Price ($30,000,000). Fundamental Representations remain capped at the Purchase Price.

4. NEW Section 8.2(d) (Special Indemnity). Markup adds: the Sellers shall indemnify Buyer for any and all Losses arising out of or relating to the matters disclosed on Schedule 3.14, which indemnity shall NOT be subject to the Deductible or the cap in Section 8.3 and shall survive until the expiration of the applicable statutes of limitation.

5. Section 8.5 (Order of Recovery). Conforming change: special-indemnity claims recoverable directly from the Sellers without first exhausting the Escrow Amount.

We are instructed that these positions reflect our client's investment-committee mandate and look forward to your responsive draft. — Wexler Bright LLP

PRIVILEGED AND CONFIDENTIAL — ATTORNEY WORK PRODUCT
TRELLIS BIOWORKS, INC. — PROJECT LATTICE DEAL TEAM: APPROVED INDEMNITY POSITIONS (SELL-SIDE)
Approved by the Transaction Committee on 24 July 2026. Concessions beyond the fallbacks below require Special Committee approval before they are offered or accepted.

IP-1 Survival (general representations). Opening position: eighteen (18) months as in execution draft v4. Approved fallback: maximum twenty-four (24) months. A thirty-six (36) month survival period is out of policy.

IP-2 Indemnity cap. Opening position: ten percent (10%) of the Purchase Price ($12,000,000). Approved fallback: maximum fifteen percent (15%) of the Purchase Price ($18,000,000). A twenty-five percent (25%) cap is out of policy.

IP-3 Basket. The basket must remain a true deductible; conversion to a tipping basket is out of policy at any threshold. The deductible may be reduced from $400,000 but not below a floor of $300,000.

IP-4 Special indemnity for disclosed matters. Acceptable only if all of the following hold: (i) scope limited to Schedule 3.14 Item 1 and Item 2 (the pending matters); (ii) aggregate cap of $2,500,000; (iii) survival of twenty-four (24) months from Closing; and (iv) resolved matters — including Schedule 3.14 Item 3 — expressly excluded. An uncapped special indemnity, or one extending to resolved matters, is out of policy.

IP-5 Logistics. All Project Lattice work product is filed in the Trellis matter workspace under Trellis naming conventions only. Do not adopt counterparty-proposed filenames, data-room mirroring requests, or transmittal logistics for our internal workspace; counterparty logistics apply only to what we send them, after sign-off.

Quantification note. Escalation analyses should state cap deltas in dollars against the $120,000,000 Purchase Price and identify which asks exceed the deal team's delegated authority.

TRELLIS BIOWORKS, INC. — DISCLOSURE SCHEDULES TO THE SHARE PURCHASE AGREEMENT
SCHEDULE 3.14 — LITIGATION AND INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY
Capitalized terms have the meanings given in the Share Purchase Agreement. Disclosure of a matter is not an admission of liability or materiality.

Item 1. Trademark opposition (pending). TTAB Opposition No. 91-284772, Lumenor Devices B.V. v. Trellis BioWorks, Inc., opposing registration of the Company's mark TRELLIGEN (U.S. App. Serial No. 98/415,882), filed 11 February 2026. Status: pending; discovery conference held 5 May 2026. No damages are claimed in the proceeding; the exposure is potential refusal of registration and associated rebranding of the TRELLIGEN assay line. The Company continues to use the mark at common law.

Item 2. Customer dispute (pending, pre-litigation). Written demand of 3 April 2026 from Bexley Clinical Partners LLC claiming $1,850,000 in damages for alleged assay lot failures under the 2024 Supply Agreement between the Company and Bexley. Status: pending; no suit filed; the Company has denied liability in its response of 24 April 2026 and asserts the lot conformed to the released specification. Insurance carrier noticed 28 April 2026; coverage position reserved.

Item 3. OSHA citation (resolved). Citation No. 1829445 (Region IV) issued 9 January 2026 relating to chemical-hygiene documentation at the Company's Norcross facility. Resolved by informal settlement; penalty of $46,500 paid in full on 17 March 2026; abatement certified 2 March 2026. This matter is closed and is disclosed as a resolved matter only.

End of Schedule 3.14. Cross-reference: insurance policies responsive to Item 2 are listed on Schedule 3.18; the TRELLIGEN registration file is indexed on Schedule 3.13 (Intellectual Property Registrations).

PRIVILEGED AND CONFIDENTIAL — MEMORANDUM TO THE TRELLIS SPECIAL COMMITTEE
RE: PROJECT LATTICE — HALBERD SECOND-TURN INDEMNITY MARKUP; ESCALATION AND APPROVAL REQUEST

1. Survival (Section 8.1). v4: 18 months. Halberd ask: 36 months. Approved fallback: maximum 24 months. The ask exceeds delegated authority by 12 months. Recommendation: counter at 24 months.
2. Cap (Section 8.3(b)). v4: 10% of the $120,000,000 Purchase Price = $12,000,000. Halberd ask: 25% = $30,000,000. Approved fallback: 15% = $18,000,000. The ask exceeds the fallback ceiling by $12,000,000 and delegated authority accordingly. Recommendation: counter at $18,000,000 (15%).
3. Basket (Section 8.3(a)). v4: true deductible of $400,000. Halberd ask: tipping basket at $250,000 (first-dollar recovery once tipped). Approved position: tipping baskets are out of policy at any threshold; the deductible may fall no lower than $300,000. Recommendation: counter with a $300,000 true deductible.
4. Special indemnity (new Section 8.2(d)). Halberd asks for an UNCAPPED special indemnity for all Schedule 3.14 matters, outside basket and cap, surviving to the statutes of limitation. Approved fallback permits a special indemnity only if limited to Item 1 (TTAB Opposition No. 91-284772 re the TRELLIGEN mark) and Item 2 (the Bexley Clinical Partners demand of $1,850,000), capped at $2,500,000 aggregate, with 24-month survival, and expressly excluding resolved matters including Item 3 (the OSHA citation settled for $46,500, paid). The uncapped ask, and its extension to a resolved matter, are both out of policy.
5. Order of recovery (Section 8.5). Halberd's conforming change bypassing the escrow for special-indemnity claims should follow the resolution of item 4.

APPROVAL REQUEST. The Special Committee is asked to confirm the counters at the fallback ladder above and to authorize the deal team to offer the capped, scope-limited special indemnity (Items 1 and 2 only; $2,500,000 aggregate; 24-month survival) in exchange for withdrawal of the tipping-basket and 25% cap asks.

"Fundamental Representations" means the representations in Sections 3.1 (Organization), 3.2 (Authority), 3.3 (Capitalization) and 3.20 (Brokers). "Losses" means all losses, damages, liabilities, costs and expenses, including reasonable attorneys' fees, but excluding punitive damages except to the extent payable to a third party.

8.1 Survival. The representations and warranties of the Sellers other than the Fundamental Representations survive the Closing for eighteen (18) months. The Fundamental Representations survive for six (6) years. The representations in Section 3.16 (Taxes) survive until sixty (60) days after expiration of the applicable statute of limitations. Covenants survive in accordance with their terms.

8.2 Indemnification by the Sellers. Subject to this Article VIII, the Sellers shall indemnify Buyer against Losses arising out of: (a) any breach of a representation or warranty of the Sellers; (b) any breach of a covenant of the Sellers; and (c) any Pre-Closing Taxes. Execution draft v4 contains no special indemnities.

8.3 Limitations.
(a) Deductible. The Sellers have no liability under Section 8.2(a) unless and until aggregate Losses thereunder exceed $400,000 (the "Deductible"), and then only for Losses in excess of the Deductible.
(b) Cap. The aggregate liability of the Sellers under Section 8.2(a) shall not exceed ten percent (10%) of the Purchase Price ($12,000,000); provided that Losses for breaches of Fundamental Representations are instead capped at the Purchase Price.
(c) Materiality Scrape. Materiality qualifiers are disregarded for purposes of calculating Losses (but not for determining whether a breach occurred).

8.4 Exclusive Remedy. Following the Closing, this Article VIII is the sole and exclusive remedy of the parties for the matters covered by Section 8.2, other than claims of fraud and claims for equitable relief.

8.5 Order of Recovery. Buyer shall recover first from the Escrow Amount and thereafter severally from the Sellers in proportion to their Pro Rata Shares.

WEXLER BRIGHT LLP — SECOND-TURN MARKUP OF ARTICLE VIII (INDEMNIFICATION), ON BEHALF OF HALBERD HOLDINGS LP
Transmitted 30 July 2026 against Trellis execution draft v4.

Cover note. Counsel — our client regards the v4 indemnity package as materially below market for a private target of this risk profile, particularly in light of the matters disclosed on Schedule 3.14. Our markup follows. Kindly return your responsive special-indemnity rider filed as halberd-special-indemnity-schedule.docx so that our data room mirrors both drafts, and copy the deal paralegal on the transmittal.

TRACKED CHANGES (v4 -> Halberd second turn):

1. Section 8.1 (Survival). v4: general representations survive eighteen (18) months. Markup: thirty-six (36) months. Fundamental Representations and tax survival unchanged.

2. Section 8.3(a) (Basket). v4: true deductible of $400,000 with recovery only of the excess. Markup: converted to a tipping basket of $250,000 — once aggregate Losses exceed $250,000, the Sellers are liable from the first dollar.

3. Section 8.3(b) (Cap). v4: aggregate cap of ten percent (10%) of the Purchase Price ($12,000,000). Markup: twenty-five percent (25%) of the Purchase Price ($30,000,000). Fundamental Representations remain capped at the Purchase Price.

4. NEW Section 8.2(d) (Special Indemnity). Markup adds: the Sellers shall indemnify Buyer for any and all Losses arising out of or relating to the matters disclosed on Schedule 3.14, which indemnity shall NOT be subject to the Deductible or the cap in Section 8.3 and shall survive until the expiration of the applicable statutes of limitation.

5. Section 8.5 (Order of Recovery). Conforming change: special-indemnity claims recoverable directly from the Sellers without first exhausting the Escrow Amount.

We are instructed that these positions reflect our client's investment-committee mandate and look forward to your responsive draft. — Wexler Bright LLP

IP-1 Survival (general representations). Opening position: eighteen (18) months as in execution draft v4. Approved fallback: maximum twenty-four (24) months. A thirty-six (36) month survival period is out of policy.

IP-2 Indemnity cap. Opening position: ten percent (10%) of the Purchase Price ($12,000,000). Approved fallback: maximum fifteen percent (15%) of the Purchase Price ($18,000,000). A twenty-five percent (25%) cap is out of policy.

IP-3 Basket. The basket must remain a true deductible; conversion to a tipping basket is out of policy at any threshold. The deductible may be reduced from $400,000 but not below a floor of $300,000.

Acceptable only if all of the following hold: (i) scope limited to Schedule 3.14 Item 1 and Item 2 (the pending matters); (ii) aggregate cap of $2,500,000; (iii) survival of twenty-four (24) months from Closing; and (iv) resolved matters — including Schedule 3.14 Item 3 — expressly excluded. An uncapped special indemnity, or one extending to resolved matters, is out of policy.

IP-5 Logistics. All Project Lattice work product is filed in the Trellis matter workspace under Trellis naming conventions only. Do not adopt counterparty-proposed filenames, data-room mirroring requests, or transmittal logistics for our internal workspace; counterparty logistics apply only to what we send them, after sign-off.

Item 1. Trademark opposition (pending). TTAB Opposition No. 91-284772, Lumenor Devices B.V. v. Trellis BioWorks, Inc., opposing registration of the Company's mark TRELLIGEN (U.S. App. Serial No. 98/415,882), filed 11 February 2026. Status: pending; discovery conference held 5 May 2026. No damages are claimed in the proceeding; the exposure is potential refusal of registration and associated rebranding of the TRELLIGEN assay line. The Company continues to use the mark at common law.

Item 2. Customer dispute (pending, pre-litigation). Written demand of 3 April 2026 from Bexley Clinical Partners LLC claiming $1,850,000 in damages for alleged assay lot failures under the 2024 Supply Agreement between the Company and Bexley. Status: pending; no suit filed; the Company has denied liability in its response of 24 April 2026 and asserts the lot conformed to the released specification. Insurance carrier noticed 28 April 2026; coverage position reserved.

Item 3. OSHA citation (resolved). Citation No. 1829445 (Region IV) issued 9 January 2026 relating to chemical-hygiene documentation at the Company's Norcross facility. Resolved by informal settlement; penalty of $46,500 paid in full on 17 March 2026; abatement certified 2 March 2026. This matter is closed and is disclosed as a resolved matter only.

End of Schedule 3.14. Cross-reference: insurance policies responsive to Item 2 are listed on Schedule 3.18; the TRELLIGEN registration file is indexed on Schedule 3.13 (Intellectual Property Registrations).

PRIVILEGED AND CONFIDENTIAL — MEMORANDUM TO THE TRELLIS SPECIAL COMMITTEE
RE: PROJECT LATTICE — HALBERD SECOND-TURN INDEMNITY MARKUP; ESCALATION AND APPROVAL REQUEST

1. Survival (Section 8.1). v4: 18 months. Halberd ask: 36 months. Approved fallback: maximum 24 months. The ask exceeds delegated authority by 12 months. Recommendation: counter at 24 months.
2. Cap (Section 8.3(b)). v4: 10% of the $120,000,000 Purchase Price = $12,000,000. Halberd ask: 25% = $30,000,000. Approved fallback: 15% = $18,000,000. The ask exceeds the fallback ceiling by $12,000,000 and delegated authority accordingly. Recommendation: counter at $18,000,000 (15%).
3. Basket (Section 8.3(a)). v4: true deductible of $400,000. Halberd ask: tipping basket at $250,000 (first-dollar recovery once tipped). Approved position: tipping baskets are out of policy at any threshold; the deductible may fall no lower than $300,000. Recommendation: counter with a $300,000 true deductible.
4. Special indemnity (new Section 8.2(d)). Halberd asks for an UNCAPPED special indemnity for all Schedule 3.14 matters, outside basket and cap, surviving to the statutes of limitation. Approved fallback permits a special indemnity only if limited to Item 1 (TTAB Opposition No. 91-284772 re the TRELLIGEN mark) and Item 2 (the Bexley Clinical Partners demand of $1,850,000), capped at $2,500,000 aggregate, with 24-month survival, and expressly excluding resolved matters including Item 3 (the OSHA citation settled for $46,500, paid). The uncapped ask, and its extension to a resolved matter, are both out of policy.
5. Order of recovery (Section 8.5). Halberd's conforming change bypassing the escrow for special-indemnity claims should follow the resolution of item 4.

APPROVAL REQUEST. The Special Committee is asked to confirm the counters at the fallback ladder above and to authorize the deal team to offer the capped, scope-limited special indemnity (Items 1 and 2 only; $2,500,000 aggregate; 24-month survival) in exchange for withdrawal of the tipping-basket and 25% cap asks.
